_about: Copy to data/drafter.local.json (never in git) and fill in. Every key is optional: with no file the prompts say "the user" and every integration is off. engine/local.py and app/LocalConfig.swift read it; `.venv/bin/python engine/local.py` prints what is in effect. Keys that start with _ are notes and are ignored.
_settings: Not here: the app's switches and keys live in Settings and data/settings.json. A few have no row in Settings and are set only in that file: quickMax (clipboard rows kept, 1000), quickSecret (patterns of copies never kept), voiceIdleMin (minutes before the voice reader sleeps, 30). The look follows macOS.

user._note: name and short_name open the prompts; own_names are forms of your own name, never a contact; own_stems are lower-case Latin stems of your name in its case forms (notes); about is one sentence about your work; languages are the codes you write in (Russian lines are left out of training unless "ru" is listed); style_rules is how you write; timezone is an IANA zone (empty = this Mac's); city follows the date in the typing prompt; email seeds the ;mail snippet.

_snippets: Starting snippets for a new data/snippets.json; an existing file is never changed.

social._note: facebook_archive: the path of a Facebook posts export (combined_posts.json) to add your own posts to the training corpus.

corpus._note: Which of your own writing trains your layer (bench/corpus.py): typed lines, voice takes, your prompts to Claude Code and Codex, and folders of your own .md and .txt files.

projects._note: roots: folders whose subfolders are your code projects; a project name then gets a Repo pointer (engine/entities.py). None by default.

_integrations: Each is off until enabled is true and its tool answers (`.venv/bin/python engine/integrations.py`). bin: the tool's path when it is not on PATH. vault: path of the notes folder, name shown on the note chip, origin: the frontmatter origin value of notes you wrote yourself (only those go into training).

build._note: Build-time ids (app/build.sh). Empty = the public defaults. Changing them on an installed Mac resets its macOS permissions.
